layers.note: A tall deciduous shrub of open subalpine forest, tree-clump edges, old burns and avalanche tracks.

moisture.note: Moderately dry to moist, acid ground.

elevation_m.note: From about 900 m to high mountains (FEIS, Simonin 2000); to about 2,000 m and more in the Cascades.

shade_tolerance.note: Fairly shade tolerant; fruits best in openings (FEIS, Simonin 2000).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −18 to 3 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 7 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −40 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 9 to 19 °C; gone below 7 °C, where summers are too short, and above 23 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 900 to 4,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 600.

degree_days_5.note: About 300 to 2,400 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 150.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Thinleaf (big) huckleberry grows from British Columbia and Nunavut south through the Cascade and Olympic Mountains to California and Arizona and east to Ontario, Wyoming, South Dakota and Minnesota, with outliers in Michigan (FEIS, Simonin 2000). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
